`spawnSync(program, args)` uses no shell (`harness/scripts/pr-freeze.ts:361-362`), and just forwards positional arguments through quoted `"$@"` (`justfile:14,213-214`). PR titles are not read; branch/body text does not become subprocess options or worktree paths. Delivers content travels through stdin. PR numbers are validated before subprocesses; SHA values originate in exact-ref Git output, not PR prose, and GitHub disagreement prevents worktree creation.

The fetch is `git fetch -q --no-tags origin <main-sha> <pr-head-sha>` (`pr-freeze.ts:235`). It disables tag following and supplies no destination refspecs. Under normal configuration this does not move branches or remote-tracking refs, but it writes FETCH_HEAD and objects, even potentially before head-disagreement refusal. No explicit refmap override is supplied; this is not an unconditional all-ref guarantee under arbitrary local configuration.

New worktree paths derive from the local repository parent, validated PR number and Git-produced SHA prefix, with `--detach` at the full SHA (`pr-freeze.ts:325-335`). Reuse does not reset, clean or check out an existing worktree.

**Reviewer-integrity notes, not exploitable security findings:** reuse checks HEAD and filename suffix, not detached state or cleanliness (`pr-freeze.ts:167-172`); boolean `--worktree` is supported, an explicit destination is not (`387-393`); the missing-Delivers-parser fallback does not independently require a named successful delivers check (`305-311`). Current-head delivers receipts did pass, but generic green checks alone would not prove that fallback claim.

No credential/token literals, private owner/name identities, private content or foreign machine-layout paths found. Own pij layout/product references and generic fixtures are permitted. No daemon or migration changes.
